craft.description: Full confirmed-brief-then-build flow. Runs multi-round shape discovery first, resolves visual probe and north-star mock gates when available, then builds and visually iterates. Use when building a new feature end-to-end.

teach.description: Repairs missing strategic design context when LunaCraft is blocked. Full project initialization belongs to project-context, while DESIGN.md generation belongs to /lunacraft document.

document.description: Generate a DESIGN.md file that captures the current visual design system. Auto-extracts colors, typography, spacing, radii, and component patterns from the codebase, then asks the user to confirm descriptive language for atmosphere and color character. Follows the Google Stitch DESIGN.md format so the file is tool-compatible. Use when you need a visual design spec an AI agent can follow to stay on-brand.

extract.description: Pull reusable patterns, components, and design tokens into the design system. Identifies repeated patterns and consolidates them. Use when you have drift across the codebase and want to bring things back to a consistent system.

live.description: Interactive live variant mode. Select elements in the browser, pick a design action, and get AI-generated HTML+CSS variants hot-swapped via HMR. Requires a running dev server. Use when you want to visually experiment with design alternatives in real time.

audit.description: Run technical quality checks across accessibility, performance, theming, responsive design, and anti-patterns. Generates a scored report with P0-P3 severity ratings and actionable plan. Use when the user wants an accessibility check, performance audit, or technical quality review.

critique.description: Evaluate design from a UX perspective, assessing visual hierarchy, information architecture, emotional resonance, cognitive load, and overall quality with quantitative scoring, persona-based testing, automated anti-pattern detection, and actionable feedback. Use when the user asks to review, critique, evaluate, or give feedback on a design or component.

improve.description: Diagnose and fix structural/functional design problems. Runs critique diagnostics, presents a checkpoint summary of issues found, then sequentially fixes confirmed issues via focused internal passes (color, typography, layout, complexity, copy, responsive, performance, intensity, production gaps, onboarding). Use when something looks wrong, weak, or broken in the design.

elevate.description: Assess what's flat or lifeless in a structurally sound design, then add boldness, personality, and ambition. Runs a lightweight assessment across intensity, personality, and ambition, then dispatches to focused internal passes. Not for motion-only work — use animate after polish.

enhance.description: One-shot improve then elevate: diagnose and fix structural problems, then add boldness and personality on the repaired structure. Single merged summary (checkpoint only for topology/media changes), single detect reconcile, single close-out. Never opens a browser. Use when the user wants one pass that both fixes and emboldens.

redesign.description: Renegotiate the visual identity of an existing surface. Presents 2-3 genuinely different named direction concepts, waits for the user to pick, rewrites DESIGN.md first, then applies the new system primitives-first. Use when the user rejects the current look at identity level (doesn't feel like the brand, looks generic, still looks like a donor project). Never satisfied by an in-system enhance.

polish.description: Design-lock QA pass: pixel alignment, spacing consistency, interaction state completeness, design-system compliance, responsive checks, and code cleanup. Nothing new gets added — everything that exists gets refined. Run before animate.

animate.description: Mandatory post-polish motion pass. Run animate.md Steps 0-4: audit, implement all 6 layers, code-level verify (browser only if explicitly requested), emit close-out block. Non-destructive. Not a single fade-in.
